text.p: Following are some of the major events to have occurred on January 20 in history.
1320 - Wladislaw I, also known as Wladislaw the Short, was crowned king of Poland. In defeating the Knights of the Teutonic Order, he created strong foundations for one Polish nation.
1327 - King Edward II of England was forced to abdicate by powerful barons in favour of his son Edward III.

1612 - Rudolf II, Holy Roman Emperor from 1576, died. Suffering from depression, he was unable to reconcile Roman Catholic and Protestant factions which eventually led to the Thirty Years War. He was succeeded by his bother Matthias.
1649 - British king Charles I was brought before a high court of justice at Westminster Hall on charges of treason following the civil war against parliamentarian forces.
1745 - Charles VII, Holy Roman Emperor from 1742, died. He was also elector of Bavaria.

1763 - Wolfe Tone, Irish Nationalist, born. He made several attempts to overthrow English rule in Ireland and was captured in Donegal after leading French forces. Condemned to be hanged, he cut his own throat in prison.
1778 - Captain James Cook discovered Hawaii when he landed first at Waimea on Kauai Island.
1841 - After lengthy talks between Britain and China concerning the Opium Wars, the convention of Chuanbi was signed by which Hong Kong island was ceded to the British by China.
1896 - George Burns, U.S. comedy actor, born as Nathan Birnbaum. Entertainer and film actor who late in life won an Oscar for the 1975 film "The Sunshine Boys".
1918 - In World War One, the German light cruiser Breslau was sunk by a succession of mines outside the Dardanelles.
1920 - Federico Fellini, Italian film director, born. Famed for his controversial "La Dolce Vita", as well as "La Strada" and "Otto e Mezzo" ("8-1/2").
1936 - British King George V died. He was succeeded by his son Edward VIII who caused a crisis later the same year by abdicating.

1942 - Nazi leaders of the security police and various ministries met at the Wannsee conference to set up the bureaucratic apparatus for the Final Solution and complete the systematic destruction of the Jews.
1944 - In a short air raid on Berlin with 769 bombers, the RAF dropped some 2,300 tons of bombs.
1945 - With his inauguration, Franklin Delano Roosevelt began a record fourth term in office as president of the U.S.
1961 - John F. Kennedy was inaugurated as the 35th president of the United States. He was elected by the closest vote ever and he was the youngest presidential nominee elected.
1973 - Inauguration of President Nixon for a second term. He was the first president to resign from office after the Watergate scandal.

1973 - Dr Amilcar Cabral, Guinea-Bissau Nationalist leader, assassinated in Conakry. He founded the PAIGC (African Independence Party of Guinea and Cape Verde), the organisation that fought Portuguese colonial rule.
1981 - Ronald Reagan became president of the United States at the age of 69 and 349 days. He was the oldest president to take office.
1981 - Fifty-two American hostages seized in their embassy in Tehran were released after 444 days in captivity.
1984 - Johnny Weissmuller, U.S. athlete and actor, died. Olympic swimming champion who set many records, he was mainly famed for his film appearances as Tarzan.
1987 - Terry Waite, the Archbishop of Canterbury's special envoy in Lebanon, was kidnapped. He was not released until November 1991.
1992 - An A-230 Airbus crashed into mountains south of Strasbourg, France, killing 87 of the 96 people on board.

1996 - Palestinians voted for the first time in elections that consolidated PLO chief Yasser Arafat's rule of the West Bank and Gaza under a peace deal with Israel. He became the first democratically-elected leader of the Palestinian people with 88.1 percent of the vote.
